newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Cho Hung FRN happens.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Cho Hung FRN happens.

text.p: Asian debt markets were sleepy on Thursday, with Cho Hung Bank's floating rate note the only issue launched.
The three-year paper pays a coupon of 20 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR). With fees, the all-in return is 23.3 basis points.
That is tighter than the all-in paid on Hanil Bank's three-year FRN launched about three weeks ago, which was roughly 26 basis points.
Both banks are rated A3 by Moody's Investors Service.
Otherwise, Asian bankers said Russia's heavily roadshowed international bond issue, its first since 1917, is likely to attract Korean investors who are especially keen on high yield issues.
Russia's US$1.0 billion five-year bond will be priced to yield 345 basis points over comparable Treasuries.

In news from Hong Kong, U.S. company General Electric Capital Corp's Hong Kong branch was assigned an A-plus long-term local currency and Single-A long-term foreign currency counterparty rating by Standard and Poor's Corp.

In other debt developments, a panel of experts speaking on Reuters Financial Television agreed that growing demand from Asian companies for longer-term funding will contribute significantly to the development of local currency bond markets in the region.
Infrastructure funding needs have been widely regarded as the prime engine of growth for Asian debt markets.
"I don't think that it is just infrastructure that is driving the demand side of the bond market," said Gautam Kaji, managing director at the World Bank.

"I think that broadly based investment is going to be many multiples of the numbers we keep talking about in terms of infrastructure, and I think that it is the aggregate demand for term finance that we have to look at," he said.
